items.why: The after capture is almost empty: the whole pricing table and FAQ disappeared from the page text, which looks like a rendering failure rather than a real change.

Only typo fixes in the FAQ text; prices and plans are the same.
Figma Specs beta went from available on paid seats to available on all seats.

record.short: Figma Specs beta is now available on all seats instead of paid seats only.
record.headline: Figma opened its Specs beta to all seats, not just paid seats, with no change to seat prices.
record.who: Anyone with a Figma seat, including seats that were previously excluded from Specs.
record.read: Figma is widening access to a beta product to build usage before it settles on packaging. Buzz is already on all seats, so this follows the same pattern. Whether Specs stays on every seat after the beta is unknown.
record.caveat: The page gives no reason or end date for the beta access.

items.why: Enterprise plan now lists GitHub Copilot access and Agent governance as included; the $21 per user per month price is unchanged.

record.short: Enterprise (still $21 per user per month) now lists GitHub Copilot access and Agent governance as included.
record.headline: GitHub’s pricing page now says Enterprise includes access to GitHub Copilot and lists Agent governance, at the same $21 per user per month.
record.who: GitHub Enterprise customers. The page does not say whether existing customers get Copilot automatically.
record.stated: GitHub Enterprise now includes access to GitHub Copilot.
record.read: GitHub is pulling Copilot into the Enterprise seat, which makes the $21 seat a broader AI platform bundle and makes it harder to compare against Copilot sold alone. It also nudges Enterprise buyers toward governance features for agents.
record.caveat: The page was heavily re-laid out in the same capture. It does not show Copilot usage allowances for Enterprise, and the separate GitHub Copilot add-on card is still shown.

items.why: Marketing statistic changed from $2/year to $2K/year in a placeholder-driven savings line; not a pricing change.
Public Cloud instances no longer include an IPv4 address by default; a public IPv4 address is now an option.

record.short: Public Cloud instances no longer include an IPv4 address by default; it becomes an optional add.
record.headline: OVHcloud’s price page now says instances do not include an IPv4 address by default, where it used to say they did apart from Local Zone instances.
rows: Not included; available as an option
record.who: Customers ordering Public Cloud instances. The page does not say whether existing instances are affected.
record.read: IPv4 addresses are scarce and getting costlier, so cloud providers are moving them from a hidden cost inside the instance price to a separate line. Expect the effective price of an instance with a public address to rise even if the listed hourly rate stays put.
record.caveat: The page does not show the price of the IPv4 option, which is shown in the Control Panel at order time. Listed instance prices look unchanged. The AI Training and AI Deploy descriptions also dropped their per minute billing wording, which may or may not be a billing change.

items.why: Core and Pro plan highlight lists were rewritten with taglines and reordered; prices are unchanged and the page does not show a real limit being removed.

record.short: The $29 Roleplay learner-seat add-on is gone, and Starter and Pro now list Syren video allowances (~2 and ~7 videos).
record.headline: Synthesia dropped the Roleplay learner-seat add-on and now shows Syren video allowances on Starter and Pro, plus 1 promo Syren video on the free Basic plan.
record.who: Teams that bought Roleplay learner seats, and Starter and Pro subscribers using AI video.
record.read: Synthesia seems to be folding AI-generated Syren video into the credit plans and removing a separately priced training add-on. Whether roleplay moved elsewhere or was retired is not clear from the page.
record.caveat: The yearly view also showed a $25 learner seat that was removed. The API tab with Interactive Avatars and Dubbing API rates is also missing from the after capture, which may be a page change or a capture issue. The free-plan FAQ answer was also shortened.
